stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: When a pathogen breaches the skin, the innate immune system dispatches several kinds of first responders. These include neutrophils, which engulf bacteria within minutes of an infection; macrophages, which digest cellular debris and release chemical signals that summon reinforcements______ natural killer cells, which destroy host cells already infected by a virus; and dendritic cells, which carry fragments of the invader to nearby lymph nodes.
explanation: This sentence lists four cell types, and each one carries its own 'which' clause set off by a comma. Because the items already contain commas, the list has to be separated by semicolons, and the writer does that everywhere else ('infection;' and 'virus;'). A semicolon after 'reinforcements' keeps the separators consistent and marks where the macrophage item ends and the natural killer item begins.

A.why: You looked only at the words around the blank, where a comma seems natural, and didn't check how the rest of the list is punctuated. The items contain internal commas and the other items are separated by semicolons, so a comma here blurs where one item stops and the next starts.

B.why: A colon introduces a list, an explanation, or an example. Natural killer cells don't explain macrophages; they are just the next item, so a colon in the middle of the series makes no sense.

D.why: A single dash works like a colon and marks an explanation or a sudden break. Nothing here is an explanation, and a dash doesn't match the semicolons that separate the other items.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Exercise physiologists who tracked 140 competitive marathoners over two seasons found three habits shared by the fastest finishers: cutting weekly mileage, often by as much as 40 percent, in the three weeks before a race; taking in carbohydrates at fixed intervals rather than only when hungry or fatigued______ and running the first half of the course slightly slower than the second.
explanation: The first habit contains a comma-bound interruption ('often by as much as 40 percent'), so the writer separates the items with semicolons, as the semicolon after 'race' shows. The blank comes between the second and third items, so it needs a semicolon to match. A semicolon before the final 'and' is standard in a list like this.

B.why: You saw the 'and' after the blank and used a comma, as you would in a simple list. This list already uses a semicolon between items because the first item has internal commas, so the separator before the last item has to be a semicolon too.

C.why: A colon has already introduced the list after 'finishers.' A second colon between two items doesn't introduce anything and splits the series at a point where no explanation follows.

D.why: A period ends the sentence after the second habit and leaves 'and running the first half…' as a fragment with no subject or main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Field linguists documenting an endangered language usually try to record three kinds of material: word lists, which capture basic vocabulary such as kinship terms and numbers______ narratives, which reveal how speakers link clauses into extended stories; and everyday conversations, which show the language as it is actually used between people who know each other well.
explanation: The blank is the first separator in the list, so you can't copy one from earlier in the sentence. You have to read ahead. The next item ends with 'stories;', and every item contains a comma before its 'which' clause. Items that contain commas are separated by semicolons, so a semicolon after 'numbers' is required.

A.why: This is the trap. The blank comes before any other list separator, so a comma looks fine if you read only up to this point. Read ahead and you'll see the items have internal commas and are separated by semicolons, so a comma here makes it unclear where the first item ends.

B.why: A colon already introduces the list after 'material.' A second colon would treat 'narratives' as an explanation of 'word lists' when it is really the next item.

C.why: A period cuts the list off after the first item and leaves 'narratives, which reveal…; and everyday conversations…' as a fragment with no main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: When the Halvorsen survey team redrew the region's coastal charts in 1932, it corrected errors in three areas: the northern inlets, previously shown as a single bay; the offshore shoals, some of which had been plotted nearly a mile too far east______ and the harbor channel, whose depth had been measured at low tide in some sections and at high tide in others.
explanation: Each of the three areas is followed by a descriptive phrase set off by a comma, so the writer separates the items with semicolons, as 'bay;' shows. The blank separates the second item (the shoals) from the third (the harbor channel), so it takes a semicolon as well.

A.why: 'Too far east, and the harbor channel' sounds fine on its own, so you decided from the local words. But the list is already separated by semicolons because its items contain commas, and a comma here doesn't match that pattern.

C.why: A colon would present the harbor channel as an explanation of the shoal errors. It is a separate third area, and the list has already been introduced by the colon after 'areas.'

D.why: A single dash signals an explanation or an abrupt break, like a colon. The harbor channel is simply the next item, and a dash doesn't match the semicolon already separating the items.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In a twelve-week trial involving 380 adults with mildly elevated blood pressure, nutrition researchers scored each participant's diet on intake of dietary fiber, potassium______ and calcium; diets high in all three nutrients were associated with the largest reductions in systolic pressure by the end of the trial.
explanation: The list here is three single nouns with no internal punctuation, and the writer has already separated the first two with a comma ('fiber, potassium'). Simple items take commas, so you match that separator and put a comma after 'potassium.' The semicolon after 'calcium' isn't part of the list. It joins two independent clauses.

A.why: You spotted the later semicolon and assumed it separated list items. It actually separates two complete sentences. The list items are single words and the writer already used a comma after 'fiber,' so a semicolon here doesn't match.

B.why: A colon must follow a complete thought and introduce what comes after it. Putting one between the second and third items of a simple list breaks up the series for no reason.

D.why: A period ends the sentence after 'potassium' and leaves 'and calcium' as a fragment cut off from the list it belongs to.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Health officials credit the county's rise in childhood vaccination rates to three measures introduced in 2023: mobile clinics, which visited the neighborhoods with the lowest coverage first; text-message reminders, sent to parents in five languages______ and extended walk-in hours at local pharmacies, which now stay open until 9 p.m. on weekdays.
explanation: Each measure is followed by a descriptive phrase or clause set off by a comma, and the writer separates the measures with a semicolon after 'first.' The blank falls between the second measure (text-message reminders) and the third (walk-in hours), so it needs a semicolon to match.

A.why: The comma inside the second item ('reminders, sent to parents…') makes another comma look natural here. That's the trap. The list is separated by semicolons, and a comma would merge the second and third measures.

C.why: The colon after '2023' has already introduced the list. Another colon between two items would wrongly present the pharmacy hours as an explanation of the text messages.

D.why: A period ends the sentence after the second measure and leaves 'and extended walk-in hours…' as a fragment with no main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Meteorologists describe the life of an ordinary thunderstorm in three stages: the cumulus stage, in which warm, rising air builds the cloud steadily upward; the mature stage, marked by heavy rain and by updrafts and downdrafts operating side by side______ and the dissipating stage, in which downdrafts dominate, the supply of warm air is cut off, and the storm gradually weakens.
explanation: All three stages carry descriptions with internal commas, and the third even contains its own small comma series ('downdrafts dominate, the supply… is cut off, and the storm… weakens'). The writer therefore separates the stages with semicolons, as 'upward;' shows. The blank divides the mature stage from the dissipating stage, so it takes a semicolon.

B.why: A comma looks fine before 'and the dissipating stage' if you read only nearby. But the list is built from items with internal commas and is already separated by a semicolon, so a comma makes it hard to tell where the mature stage ends.

C.why: A colon would present the dissipating stage as an explanation of the mature stage. It is simply the next stage in the series, and the list was already introduced by the colon after 'stages.'

D.why: A single dash works like a colon and signals an explanation or a break in thought. Here it interrupts a series that is separated by semicolons, so it doesn't match.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The 2021 redesign of Corliss Avenue, long one of the city's most dangerous corridors, introduced protected bike lanes, separated from traffic by concrete planters; wider sidewalks, which now accommodate café seating in warmer months______ raised crosswalks at four intersections near the elementary school; and a bus-only lane during morning and evening rush hours.
explanation: This sentence has a lot of commas, including the interrupter 'long one of the city's most dangerous corridors,' so you need the semicolons to see where each item stops. The first item ends at 'planters;' and the third at 'school;'. The blank separates the second item (wider sidewalks) from the third (raised crosswalks), so it must be a semicolon too.

A.why: A colon would present the raised crosswalks as an explanation of the wider sidewalks. They are a separate change in the same list, so a colon makes no sense between these items.

B.why: The comma before 'which now accommodate…' and the comma-heavy opening make one more comma look harmless. That's the trap. The items are separated by semicolons, and a comma here would run the sidewalks and crosswalks together.

C.why: A period ends the sentence partway through the list and leaves 'raised crosswalks…; and a bus-only lane…' as a fragment with no subject or verb.
